problems.title: A rational equation with two roots
problems.question: Solve $x/(x-2)=1/(x^2-2x)$ and find the root product.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Multiply by $x(x-2)$ to get $x^2=1$. Both roots $1,-1$ satisfy the restrictions.
Their product is $-1$.

problems.title: A range for a linear expression
problems.question: $a\in[-2,1]$, $b\in[-3,5]$. Find the range of $2a-3b$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The expression increases with $a$ and decreases with $b$.
steps: Continuity gives every value between the endpoints.

problems.title: A diagonal divides a trapezoid midline
problems.question: A diagonal divides the midline into pieces differing by 2. The bases have ratio $1:3$. Find the midline.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The two pieces are half the respective bases.
steps: Write the bases $t,3t$. The pieces are $t/2,3t/2$, with difference $t=2$.
The midline is $(t+3t)/2=2t=4$.

problems.title: A quadrilateral with bisected diagonals
problems.question: One angle is $40^\circ$ and the diagonals bisect one another. Find the sum of the two largest of the other three angles.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: Bisected diagonals characterize a parallelogram; adjacent angles supplement each other.
steps: The angles are $40^\circ,140^\circ,40^\circ,140^\circ$.
The two largest remaining angles sum to $280^\circ$.

problems.title: Solve an absolute-value inequality
problems.question: Solve $|x-2|<2x+1$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The two inequalities give $x-2<2x+1$, or $x>-3$, and $x-2>-(2x+1)$, or $x>1/3$.
The combined bound $x>1/3$ also makes the right side positive, so it is sufficient.

problems.title: A radical equation with opposing sign restrictions
problems.question: How many real solutions does $\sqrt{-x}=x$ have?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The radical requires $x\le0$, while its nonnegative output requires $x\ge0$.
steps: Both restrictions force $x=0$. Direct substitution verifies it.

problems.title: A quadrilateral with both an incircle and circumcircle
problems.question: Which listed quadrilateral type can have both an inscribed and a circumscribed circle?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: An isosceles trapezoid is cyclic; it is tangential when its base sum equals its leg sum.
steps: A non-square isosceles trapezoid can satisfy both conditions. For example, bases 2 and 8 and equal legs 5 have base sum 10 equal to leg sum 10; the height is $\sqrt{25-9}=4$.
Thus an isosceles trapezoid is possible, while a rectangle, square or rhombus is not forced.
problems.answer: It can be an isosceles trapezoid (choice ე).
problems.note: This uses the usual exclusive trapezoid convention. With an inclusive definition, a square is also a right trapezoid, making the “possible right trapezoid” choice true too.

problems.title: Compare tangent and secant pieces
problems.question: A tangent is 4 cm longer than a secant’s external part and 4 cm shorter than its internal part. Find tangent length.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The tangent is positive and its external piece must be positive, so $t=8$.

problems.title: Rationalize a radical denominator
problems.question: Evaluate $2/(8-\sqrt{60})-\sqrt{15}$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The first fraction is $1/(4-\sqrt{15})=4+\sqrt{15}$. Subtracting $\sqrt{15}$ leaves 4.

problems.title: Factor with square roots
problems.question: Simplify $[(a+2\sqrt{ab}+b)/(a-b)]\cdot[(a\sqrt a-a\sqrt b)/(\sqrt{a^3}+\sqrt{a^2b})]$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: $a+2\sqrt{ab}+b=(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2$; $a-b=(\sqrt a-\sqrt b)(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)$.
steps: On the original real domain, $a>0,b\ge0,a\ne b$. The first fraction is $(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)/(\sqrt a-\sqrt b)$.
The second is $a(\sqrt a-\sqrt b)/[a(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)]$, its reciprocal. Their product is 1.

problems.title: Order three powers between zero and one
problems.question: For $0<a<1$, order $a,\sqrt a,a^2$ increasingly.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: Multiplication by a number in $(0,1)$ decreases a positive number.
steps: $a^2<a$. Also $a<\sqrt a$ because squaring the positive sides is equivalent to $a^2<a$.

problems.title: Geometric mean versus harmonic mean
problems.question: For positive $a,b$, which listed inequality must hold?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Multiply $a+b\ge2\sqrt{ab}$ by positive $\sqrt{ab}/(a+b)$.
This gives $\sqrt{ab}\ge2ab/(a+b)$. Equality holds at $a=b$.

problems.title: A line through a point above the parabola vertex
problems.question: How many intersections can $y=x^2$ have with a line through $(0,5)$?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The line is $y=mx+5$, and intersections solve $x^2-mx-5=0$.
steps: The discriminant is $m^2+20>0$ for every real slope. Hence every such line has exactly two distinct intersections.

problems.title: A section through a trapezoid’s diagonal intersection
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 3,6. Find the base-parallel section through the diagonal intersection.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The section length is the harmonic mean $2ab/(a+b)$.
steps: Similar triangles place the intersection at fraction $a/(a+b)$ of the height measured from base $a$. Parallel widths vary linearly.
Thus its width is $a+(b-a)a/(a+b)=2ab/(a+b)=36/9=4$.

problems.title: Sum of quadratic roots
problems.question: Solve $x^2-5x+6=0$ and find the root sum.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The roots are 2 and 3, with sum 5.

problems.title: Number of real roots of a quadratic
problems.question: How many real solutions can a genuine quadratic equation have?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: If $D<0$ there are no real roots; if $D=0$ one distinct real root; if $D>0$ two distinct real roots.

problems.title: A quadratic with no real roots
problems.question: If $x^2+bx+c=0$ has no real solutions, what inequality must hold?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Rearrange the discriminant condition to $b^2<4c$.

problems.title: Leg sum in a thirty-sixty triangle
problems.question: One acute angle of a right triangle is twice the other, and hypotenuse is 1. Find the leg sum.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The angles are $30^\circ,60^\circ,90^\circ$; corresponding side ratio is $1:\sqrt3:2$.
steps: The legs are $1/2$ and $\sqrt3/2$. Their sum is $(1+\sqrt3)/2$.

problems.title: Two given sides of a right triangle
problems.question: How many noncongruent right triangles can have two sides of lengths 2 and 3?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: Pythagoras; the hypotenuse is the longest side.
steps: If both are legs, the third side is $\sqrt{13}$. If 3 is the hypotenuse and 2 a leg, the other leg is $\sqrt5$.
2 cannot be the hypotenuse while another side is 3. The two valid side triples are different.

problems.title: Distance between two coordinate points
problems.question: Find the distance from $(-1,2)$ to $(3,5)$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The coordinate changes are 4 and 3. Thus $d=\sqrt{16+9}=5$.

problems.title: Leg ratio from hypotenuse projections
problems.question: The altitude to a right triangle’s hypotenuse divides it in ratio $1:2$. Find the leg ratio.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Dividing gives $a^2/b^2=p/q=1/2$. Taking positive square roots gives $a:b=1:\sqrt2$.

problems.title: Altitude from two hypotenuse pieces
problems.question: The hypotenuse is split by its altitude into lengths 8 and 18. Find the altitude.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.

problems.title: A leg and its projection
problems.question: A right triangle has one leg 3 and that leg’s hypotenuse projection 1. Find the other leg.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: $3^2=c\cdot1$ gives hypotenuse $c=9$. Then $b=\sqrt{81-9}=\sqrt{72}=6\sqrt2$.

problems.title: A common external tangent
problems.question: Externally touching circles have radii 2 and 3. Find the segment between contact points on a common external tangent.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The centre distance is 5. Thus $l=\sqrt{25-1}=\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt6$.

problems.title: A common internal tangent
problems.question: Two circles have centre distance 13 and radii 5,7. Find a common internal tangent segment.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: $l=\sqrt{169-144}=5$. The tangent exists since $13>5+7$.
